capability: Bound asynchronous action approval with target revalidation and one-winner dispatch
evidence: Pinned README, root Apache-2.0 LICENSE, design/MCP/acceptance documentation and approval/gateway implementation plus four test-source files were read as untrusted text. Eleven blobs matched Git hashes. No foreign code, tests, installer, phone connection or separate model API was executed or copied.

Static inspection of approval.go shows binding checks and one-winner decision consumption. pipeline.go binds session/device/lease/tool/argument digest, distinguishes pending from dispatch, and rechecks screen, policy and preflight under a device action lock. Documentation describes decisions outside agent tool arguments and device-access bypass limits. These observations do not establish authentication or race safety for every route, nor reproduce the source test claims.

Canonical skills/rules/agents were searched for approval, pending, expiry, stale targets, revalidation and action scope. Agent security hardening already requires exact-operation/resource authorization at the real entry point, but lacked the asynchronous continuation and target-version lifecycle. Operator approval loop already owns immutable outbound drafts, epoch binding, claims and uncertain delivery; harness construction owns recovery and evidence; E2E owns replay safety. Native copies were excluded as extra capabilities.

Added original conditional guidance to agent-security-hardening for trusted decision provenance, immutable request binding, bounded pending continuation, revocation and target revalidation serialized with admission, one-winner consumption and unknown-outcome reconciliation. Linked the existing outbound protocol rather than duplicate its implementation. Valid standing authorization remains sufficient; no source timeout, automatic re-ask, human-only policy or permission expansion was adopted.

Seven independent synthetic raw cases exercise forged consent, pending continuation, binding substitution, stale target/admission race, concurrent pickup, expiry/revocation and standing authorization with unknown dispatched outcome. These validate instruction decisions only; actual gateway authorization, race control and external delivery require implementation tests. The new requirements are not claims of an implemented ECC gateway.
reason: Extend the existing agent-runtime hardening owner with the specific missing asynchronous approval lifecycle, without a mobile-control skill, new ledger, runtime dependency or approval requirement for ordinary authorized work.
